messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT for customer 'Montauk' - high error-rate observed for VPC dedicated pool montauk-prod (region: us-west-2). Model latency spikes +5x, 23% 5xxs. Triggered at 1790123456
kevin.m: I'm on it. first look: logs show KV cache churn and OOMs on a subset of nodes. Confirming impacted tenants = montauk-prod only?
anya.k: Confirmed isolation to montauk-prod dedicated pool. No cross-tenant bleed. Affected models: monterey-7b-int8 and monterey-7b-q4_0.
sre-jen: Paging ops-oncall for live mitigation and handoff. ops-oncall are you available?
ops-oncall: Here. taking over from kevin. whats current customer impact? are customers getting 500s or slow tails?
kevin.m: Mix. ~23% 5xx, rest severe tail latency (5-30s). Errors look like "kv-cache-miss->oom" in runtime logs. attaching sample log: ```ERROR runtime: alloc failed: attempted 2GB, available 1.2GB; model monterey-7b-q4_0```
ops-oncall: Thanks. Initial plan: 1) pin montauk-prod route to monterey-7b-safe (smaller safe variant) 2) scale dedicated pool with spare nodes 3) enable strict KV prefix caching to reduce mem churn. Can infra apply pin immediately?
infra-olga: Can do pin via console or API. Suggest API to avoid UI lag. Command: `curl -X POST https://console.internal.api/routes/montauk-prod/pin -d '{"model":"monterey-7b-safe","reason":"incident 1790123456 - fallback"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'`
ops-oncall: Executing pin now.
incbot: Model pinning change submitted by ops-oncall. Rollout: immediate. Previous model will be rolled back after 1h unless explicitly unpinned.
customer-eng-ryan: FYI I told Montauk engineering we might pin to a smaller variant for stability. They asked about output quality delta. How much regression expected?
kevin.m: monterey-7b-safe is tuned for safety - ~5-8% drop in long-form coherence for some prompts, but latency/stability tradeoff is favorable. Good to communicate.
ops-oncall: Pin succeeded. Route now serving monterey-7b-safe. Observability: dropping 5xxs to 4% and p50 latency down from 1.2s to 0.6s in the first 2 minutes.
anya.k: Opening mitigation checklist: - pin route (done) - increase pool capacity (in progress) - enable strict KV (pending canary) - monitor for quality regressions (engaging customer)
ops-oncall: Kicking off pool scale: `kctl scale pool montauk-prod --replicas 3` (API started, nodes provisioning). ETA ~8-12m.
infra-olga: Provisioning new nodes now. Will attach to pool once healthy and pass runtime healthchecks.
kevin.m: Also pushing a temporary override to runtime: disable aggressive cache eviction for monterey variants to avoid thrash. Command: `PATCH /runtime/configs/kvcache -d '{"eviction_mode":"pin_by_prefix","prefixes":["/montauk/"]}'`
incbot: Runtime config change queued by kevin.m - requires approval from eng-ops to apply to production.
sre-jen: Approving runtime config. ops-oncall please apply carefully and monitor.
ops-oncall: Applied. Watching memory graphs. Early signal: memory variance stabilized on the nodes with pinned prefixes.
customer-eng-ryan: Montauk reports a subset of their high-TPS endpoints still seeing some degraded responses but much improved. They're asking for ETA to full recovery.
ops-oncall: ETA depends on new nodes coming up and cache stabilization. Expect full recovery in ~30-45m. I'll post updates every 10m.
kevin.m: Note: we'll keep the pin in place until we validate model quality against Montauk's eval set. If quality acceptable, we can propose promoting monterey-7b-safe as canary for their traffic, then gradually move back to monterey-7b-q4_0 once runtime patches land.
anya.k: Starting eval run against Montauk's regression set (on sample prompts). Will post diffs to Montauk slack channel.
sre-jen: Quick postmortem actions: create incident ticket, record root cause hypothesis (KV eviction + memory fragmentation), and schedule follow-up with infra and runtime teams.
ops-oncall: New nodes healthy, pool back to normal capacity. 5xxs down to 1.2%, p95 latency nearing baseline. Continuing to monitor for 15m.
customer-eng-ryan: Montauk thanks the team. They've asked for a permanent guardrail: automatic fallback to safe variants when error-rate >10% for >2min. Can we add a tenant-level policy?
kevin.m: We have routing policies but not per-tenant automatic fallback. We can implement a simple policy in the short term: if error_rate(tenant)>10% && duration>120s then route->safe-variant. I'll file a follow-up RFC for a proper policy config.
ops-oncall: Agreed. I'll add an incident-specific ticket to track that.
incbot: Incident 1790123456 acknowledged by ops-oncall. Severity: Sev2.
sre-jen: Handing off to post-incident owner: anya.k. Please take on the follow-ups (RFC, postmortem, customer notes).
anya.k: Taking it. I'll compile a timeline, customer impact, and follow-up action items.
ops-oncall: Closing: metrics stable for 20m, leaving pin for 24h pending eval. Will unpin only after sign-off from anya and customer. :white_check_mark:
customer-eng-ryan: Montauk requested export of the exact prompts that saw regressions for their internal QA. Anya, can you coordinate?
anya.k: Will do. Adding to postmortem.
incbot: Incident 1790123456 closed by ops-oncall at 1790127200
